content: The references provided are a comprehensive list of studies, guidelines, and frameworks addressing various aspects of tuberculosis (TB) and its comorbidities, as well as related health conditions. 1. Tanimura et al. (2014) conducted a systematic review to assess the financial burden experienced by tuberculosis patients in lowand middle-income countries. The study highlights the economic challenges faced by these patients, which can significantly impact treatment adherence and outcomes. 2. Institute for Health Metrics and Evaluation (IHME) provides a visualization hub, GBD Compare, which offers access to global burden of disease data. This tool is essential for understanding disease trends and health metrics globally. 3. FAOSTAT: Madagascar is a database providing country-specific agricultural and nutritional data, which can be critical for understanding the nutritional determinants of health in regions like Madagascar. 4. Darnton-Hill et al. (2022) explored opportunities to prevent and manage undernutrition as a strategy to amplify efforts to end tuberculosis. The study emphasizes the importance of integrating nutritional interventions into TB care. 5. India HIV Estimates 2019 Report provides detailed data on the HIV epidemic in India, which is crucial for planning and implementing collaborative TB/HIV programs. 6. Scaling up collaborative TB/HIV activities in India is a case study that examines the implementation of integrated TB and HIV services in settings with concentrated HIV epidemics. 7. WHO (2015) published a guide for monitoring and evaluating collaborative TB/HIV activities, providing a framework for assessing the effectiveness of integrated health services. 8. WHO (2018) released a practice brief on continuity and coordination of care to support the implementation of integrated, people-centered health services, aligning with the WHO framework. 9. WHO (2017) developed a handbook on using digital technologies to support tuberculosis medication adherence, emphasizing the role of technology in improving treatment outcomes. 10. University of Oslo: DHIS2 is a web-based platform for health information management, widely used for monitoring and evaluating health programs, including TB and HIV services. 11. WHO (2019) issued guidelines on digital interventions for health system strengthening, focusing on the integration of digital tools to enhance healthcare delivery. 12. WHO (2020) published consolidated HIV strategic information guidelines, emphasizing the importance of program monitoring and management to drive impact. 13. WHO (2021) released updated guidelines on rapid diagnostics for tuberculosis detection, providing evidence-based recommendations for improving TB diagnosis. 14. WHO (2022) provided updated guidelines on the treatment of drug-susceptible tuberculosis, offering detailed protocols for effective management. 15. WHO (2021) issued guidelines on managing tuberculosis in children and adolescents, addressing the unique challenges of TB care in these populations. 16. WHO (2018) published guidelines for the care and treatment of individuals with chronic hepatitis C virus infection, emphasizing the integration of viral hepatitis care into broader health services. 17. WHO (2018) also released guidelines for the prevention, care, and treatment of chronic hepatitis B infection, providing a comprehensive approach to managing this condition. 18. WHO (2019) developed a global strategy to reduce the harmful use of alcohol, addressing its impact on health and its intersection with other conditions like TB and HIV. 19. WHO (2019) published a handbook on implementing mTB-Tobacco, a program aimed at integrating tobacco cessation into TB care, highlighting the importance of addressing risk factors. 20. Rubenstein et al. (2016) discussed the intersection of HIV, prisoners, and human rights, emphasizing the need for equitable access to healthcare in marginalized populations. 21. Hanlon et al. (2014) identified challenges and opportunities for implementing integrated mental health care in lowand middle-income countries, providing insights into health system barriers. 22. Kadia et al. (2021) conducted a systematic review and meta-analysis to identify barriers and enablers of antiretroviral therapy uptake in integrated HIV and TB treatment programs in sub-Saharan Africa. 23. Workneh et al. (2016) assessed health system challenges and opportunities for integrating diabetes and tuberculosis services in Ethiopia, highlighting the need for coordinated care. 24. Navya et al. (2019) examined the linkage of TB patients to services for tobacco cessation and alcohol abuse in India, using a mixed-methods approach to identify gaps in service delivery. 25. Chileshe and Bond (2010) explored barriers to accessing antiretroviral therapy among TB/HIV co-infected patients in rural Zambia, emphasizing the need for integrated care models. 26. Li et al. (2013) conducted a qualitative study on barriers to tuberculosis care for drug users in China, identifying systemic and social challenges. 27. Kheang et al. (2019) investigated bidirectional screening for diabetes and tuberculosis in Cambodia, demonstrating the feasibility of integrated screening programs. 28. Basir et al. (2019) operationalized bidirectional screening for TB and diabetes in private healthcare clinics in Pakistan, providing a model for public-private collaboration. 29. van Crevel and Critchley (2021) discussed the interaction between diabetes and tuberculosis, translating research findings into policy and practice recommendations. 30. Aung et al. (2020) identified barriers to antiretroviral therapy uptake among HIV-infected TB patients in Myanmar, using a mixed-methods approach to inform program improvements. 31. Komba and Frumence (2021) examined barriers to implementing isoniazid preventive therapy for people living with HIV in Tanzania, highlighting health system and patient-level challenges. 32. Baja et al. (2014) conducted a situational analysis for planning coordinated TB and diabetes care programs, emphasizing the importance of integrated approaches. 33. Daftary and Padayatchi (2012) explored social constraints to TB/HIV healthcare in South Africa, providing patient perspectives on barriers to care. 34. WHO (2021) published a global list of high-burden countries for TB, MDR/RR-TB, and TB/HIV, guiding resource allocation and program planning. 35. WHO, PEPFAR, and UNAIDS (2007) developed recommendations on task shifting to optimize the health workforce for TB and HIV care. 36. South African Department of Health (2010) created a manual to guide the integration of TB/HIV services at primary healthcare facilities, providing practical implementation strategies. These references collectively provide a robust foundation for understanding and addressing the complex interplay of tuberculosis, its comorbidities, and related health conditions, with a focus on evidence-based interventions, integrated care models, and health system strengthening.
